title: Newsletter sanitizer preserves unsafe link schemes

evidence.quote: attrs_to_remove = [a for a in el.attrib if a not in self._KEEP_ATTRS]

reasoning: HTML newsletters are untrusted input. The cleaner removes scripts and non-href attributes, but any href value survives unchanged, including javascript:, data:, file:, or other non-web schemes. That sanitized HTML is then stored as article content for EPUB/PDF/web reader rendering, so a malicious newsletter can leave active links in generated output.
recommendation: When preserving href, parse and allow only http, https, mailto, and possibly relative anchors. Drop or neutralize every other scheme before serialization.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_newsletter_service.py covers comment removal, plain-text preference, HTML fallback, and parse-error resilience, but it does not assert href scheme filtering for malicious newsletter HTML.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a newsletter HTML cleaning test with 'badok' and assert the javascript href is removed while the https link remains.
minimumFixScope: app/services/newsletter_service.py sanitizer attribute handling and tests/test_newsletter_service.py.
